tier_reason: Upgraded from C: test/release-0.10.0-performance.md in the repo gives median timings of jc_voronoi 0.9/0.10 vs Boost.Polygon (Boost 1.92.0) with method stated (Apple M5 Max, Apple clang 21.0.0, -O3 -DNDEBUG, C++11 harness, seed 4, iteration counts), and the benchmark code is public (test/perftest.cpp built by test/compile_perftest.sh with -DUSE_JC_VORONOI / -DUSE_BOOST).

corrections.claimed_speedup: test/release-0.10.0-performance.md, median Voronoi generation time, jc_voronoi 0.10 vs Boost.Polygon 1.92.0: 1k random sites 178.00 us vs 649.83 us (about 3.65x, derived from page data); 10k 4.87 ms vs 6.82 ms (about 1.40x); 100k 53.95 ms vs 80.21 ms ('32.7% faster than Boost', about 1.49x); 100k pathological (issue48) 18.63 ms vs 39.25 ms ('52.5% faster', about 2.1x). Peak memory is close to Boost (104.0%, 95.2%, 98.4%, 78.4% of Boost's peak), retained memory 27.4% lower at 100k, and allocations per generation far fewer (1,187 vs 557,371 at 100k). The older README prose says Boost is '~2x as slow as the fastest algorithms' and voronoi++ 10x-15x slower; its charts and test/report.md are gone (404).
corrections.workload: 2D Voronoi diagram generation (Fortune sweep) from deterministic random point sets (1k, 10k, 100k sites, seed 4) and a 100k pathological symmetric diagonal-pair set (issue48); median time with diagram destruction included, plus peak/retained heap and allocation count; also code size and build time.
corrections.hardware: Apple M5 Max MacBook Pro, 128 GB RAM, arm64 macOS (0.10.0 release numbers); the older README numbers were on an Intel Core i7-7567U 3.50 GHz MacBook Pro, 16 GB LPDDR3
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Apple clang 21.0.0, -O3 -DNDEBUG, C++11 benchmark harness (per test/release-0.10.0-performance.md); note test/compile_perftest.sh at HEAD builds with clang++ -O2 -g
corrections.baseline: Boost.Polygon voronoi_diagram (Boost 1.92.0); also jc_voronoi 0.9.0, and in older README prose Fastjet/Fortune C, O'Sullivan C++, voronoi++
corrections.caveats: Single Apple M5 Max machine, author-run. On regular random inputs at 100k the older jc_voronoi 0.9.0 (51.22 ms) is slightly faster than 0.10.0 (53.95 ms); 0.10.0 mainly fixes pathological scaling (9.15 s to 18.63 ms). The release doc states -O3 -DNDEBUG while the committed compile_perftest.sh uses -O2 -g, so reproducing needs the stated flags. The README's older claim that Boost uses ~2.5x the memory is not borne out by the 0.10.0 data (peak memory within about 5% at random inputs). The README charts and test/report.md return 404. Boost.Polygon is not Boost.Geometry; Boost leaves edge clipping to the client.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Compiler not stated. xmake release mode set_optimize('fastest'); the 'native' option (default true in xmake.lua at HEAD) adds -march=native -ffast-math to benchmarks.comparative, so kd3 and nanoflann are built with the same flags in one binary. README recommends profile-guided optimization.
corrections.caveats: Mixed result: 39 of 132 CSV rows are slower than nanoflann, mostly the 'base' and 'fast' configurations on bbox-volume queries (medians about 0.37x and 0.61x, worst 0.01x on synthetic-anisotropic 1-NN), which is why the aabb configurations exist. Each configuration is timed in a single pass (no repetitions). nanoflann uses leaf size 10 (its default) against kd3's tuned leaf size 32; build threads are matched (nanoflann gets omp_get_max_threads()), queries are single-threaded for both. Compiler and exact CPU are not stated, no independent reproduction. Very young repo with 11 stars. Baseline nanoflann is not Boost.Geometry/CGAL/GEOS. AGPL-3.0 (network copyleft) limits embedding in closed products.

notes: All numbers in claimed_speedup re-derived from the CSV and match (132 rows; build median 3.68x, range 0.22x-6.42x; query median 1.86x, range 0.01x-5.05x; autzen 5M k=10 on-cloud row exact). License file is LICENCE.txt (AGPL-3.0), last commit 2026-09-23, 11 stars, not a fork.

tier_reason: First-party benchmark repo (concavehull-evaluation) with public code and a timing chart plus raw sub-timing lists against CGAL alpha shapes, PostGIS and Spatialite, but no hardware, compiler or flags; the peer-reviewed RA-L paper could not be opened (arxiv.org, IEEE and MDPI blocked by egress), so B is unconfirmed.

corrections.claimed_speedup: concavehull-evaluation README chart (California shape, read by eye): at about 64,000 points Polylidar about 30-40 ms, CGAL alpha shapes about 200 ms, PostGIS about 3,150 ms (no holes) and 4,100 ms (holes), Spatialite about 11,300 ms. The same README lists 30 raw sub-timing runs on caholes_64000 (64,000 points with holes): Polylidar about 36 + 4.4 + 1.0 = about 41 ms per run, CGAL triangulation plus alpha shape about 44.4 + 153 = about 197 ms, Spatialite about 235 + 135 + 10,900 = about 11,300 ms; i.e. about 4.8x faster than CGAL and about 270x faster than Spatialite (derived from page data). Robust predicates were on; disabling them gives a further 30% speedup per the README.
corrections.caveats: The benchmark measured the original 2D Polylidar (submodule thirdparty/polylidar at commit 6e25d1f, now the polylidar2d branch, tied to the RA-L 2020 paper), not the current Polylidar3D code on master, whose API differs. Evidence is a chart image and raw timing lists in a separate 4-star benchmark repo, with no hardware, compiler or flags stated. CGAL timing covers alpha shape construction plus unordered boundary edge extraction only (no polygon assembly) but also computes alpha intervals for the whole family of shapes. CGAL 4.12 and PostGIS 2.5.2 are old; PostGIS timing includes client/server round trip. The RA-L paper (doi 10.1109/LRA.2020.3002212, arXiv 2002.01886) reportedly claims more than 4x speedup over other concave polygon extraction methods but was not opened. Repo unmaintained since 2023-03.

notes: Numbers in the record match the chart; added the text sub-timings that are on the same page. arxiv.org, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and mdpi.com were egress-blocked, so the peer-reviewed paper could not be checked; a retier check to B is worth doing where arXiv is reachable. MIT, 338 stars, last commit 2023-03-13 (abandoned) confirmed.
